Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation, I'll be using the EPDS to help us understand how you're feeling and to identify any areas where we might be able to offer additional support.

The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's completely normal to experience a range of emotions after having a baby, and this assessment will help us better understand your unique experience. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and is intended to create a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Don't worry about "right" or "wrong" answers – this is all about understanding your perspective and experience.

Let's get started. The first question is: Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to, or has that changed for you lately?

Honestly, I don't laugh as much as I used to. It's like the things that used to make me happy and make me laugh just don't have the same effect on me anymore. I mean, I still find some things funny, but it's just not the same. I feel like I've been so focused on taking care of the baby and making sure everything is okay that I haven't really had the time or energy to enjoy the things I used to. And even when I do try to watch a funny movie or something, my mind just starts wandering and I start worrying about the baby or feeling guilty about not being a good enough mom. It's hard to explain, but it's just like the joy has been sucked out of things for me lately. Some days are better than others, but overall, I just don't feel like myself and I don't laugh like I used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, no... I haven't been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as I used to. It feels like everything is just so overwhelming and serious all the time now. I mean, I'll be playing with the baby or trying to do something fun, and then I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong or all the things I'm not doing right, and it just sucks the joy out of it. I feel like I'm just going through the motions a lot of the time, trying to get everything done and take care of the baby, but I'm not really enjoying it like I thought I would. And when I do try to laugh or have fun, it feels forced or like I'm just pretending to be happy. It's hard to explain, but it's just not the same as it used to be. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I feel like I've lost myself in all of this, and I don't know how to get back to being the person I used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really... I mean, I used to love looking forward to things, whether it was a night out with friends, a vacation, or just a quiet evening at home. But now, everything just feels so overwhelming and stressful. I worry about how the baby will do when we're out, or whether I'll be able to get everything ready on time, or just how exhausted I'll be. It's hard to enjoy thinking about things when I'm already feeling so tired and anxious all the time. And even when I do try to look forward to something, I just end up worrying about all the things that could go wrong. Like, we're supposed to have a family gathering next week, and instead of being excited to see everyone, I'm just stressed about how I'll get the baby ready, and how I'll manage to take care of her in a crowded house, and whether I'll be able to get her to nap... it just feels like too much. (sighing) I wish I could just feel excited and happy about things again, but it's just not the same right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yes... I do that a lot. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is fussy, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If I'm not enjoying motherhood as much as I thought I would, I think it's because I'm just not cut out for this. It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to pack an extra diaper in the diaper bag, I'll beat myself up over it for hours, thinking about how irresponsible I am and how I'm not taking good enough care of the baby. It's exhausting, and it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not good enough. (looking down, voice dropping to a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm doing everything wrong, that I'm a terrible mother. It's a really hard feeling to live with.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(sighing) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she chokes on something? What if she gets sick? What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate her development? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get really anxious. And the thing is, it's not even like I'm thinking about real problems, it's just my mind making up all these hypothetical situations that are never going to happen. But it feels so real in the moment, you know? It's hard to calm myself down and remind myself that everything is okay. (frowning) And it's not just during the day, either. At night, when I'm trying to fall asleep, my mind starts racing with all these worries and fears, and I just lie there, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. It's really hard to turn it off. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, like something bad is going to happen and I'll be responsible for not preventing it. It's a really hard way to live.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart starts racing, my hands start shaking, and I just feel like I'm going to lose control. It's like, my mind just goes into this frantic mode, and I start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I just feel so scared and overwhelmed. (taking a deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, even though there's no real danger there. And it's not just when I'm alone, either - sometimes it happens when I'm with my partner or family members, and they're all like, "What's wrong?" And I'm like, "I don't know, I just feel really scared and panicked all of a sudden." (shaking my head) It's really embarrassing, actually. And it's hard to make it stop, too. I'll try to take deep breaths, or distract myself with something else, but sometimes it just takes a while to calm down. (looking down, voice dropping to a whisper) It's like, I'm just waiting for the next time it happens, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling slowly) Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. It's like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner and friend... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll be trying to get her to stop, and the toast will be burning... and it's just like, everything is too much. (shaking my head) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? Like, I'm just managing to keep my head above water, but I'm not really in control of anything. And it's hard to ask for help, too, because I feel like I should be able to do it all on my own. (looking down, feeling a lump in my throat) But the truth is, I'm just not coping very well. I'm exhausted, and I'm stressed, and I just feel like I'm in way over my head. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I just feel like I'm drowning in all of it, and I don't know how to keep going.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just thinking about everything that's going on and feeling really unhappy. It's like, my mind won't turn off, and I just can't seem to relax. (sighing) I'll be thinking about all the things I'm not doing right, or all the things that could go wrong, and it just keeps me up. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious or scared, and I'll just lie there, feeling really overwhelmed. (looking down, feeling a sense of sadness) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I just feel really unhappy and unfulfilled, and it's affecting my sleep. I'll go to bed feeling okay, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like, I'm just not feeling like myself, and it's hard to shake that feeling. Sometimes I'll wake up in the morning, and I'll just feel so exhausted, but not just physically... emotionally, too. Like, I just don't have the energy to face the day, because I'm already feeling so drained from the night before.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump in my throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. It's just like, everything feels so overwhelming and hopeless, and I don't know how to make it better. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. Or I'll be doing something normal, like laundry or dishes, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) It's like, I'm just feeling really empty and hollow, and I don't know how to fill that back up. Sometimes I'll try to talk to my partner about it, but I just feel like I'm burdening them with my problems. And sometimes I'll try to push through it, to just put on a happy face and pretend everything is okay... but it's hard to keep that up. (sighing) Because the truth is, everything doesn't feel okay. It feels like I'm just going through the motions, like I'm just pretending to be a good mom, but really I'm just struggling to get by. (pausing, looking up) And it's hard to admit that, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy and fulfilled, like I'm supposed to be loving every minute of this. But the truth is, I'm just not. And that feels really scary and overwhelming.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, everything just feels so overwhelming and emotional, and I don't know how to process it all. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. Or I'll be talking to my partner about something, and I'll just break down in tears. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like, I'm just feeling so much emotion all the time, and I don't know how to deal with it. Sometimes I'll try to hold it in, to just push through and pretend everything is okay... but it's hard to keep that up. (looking down, feeling a lump in my throat) Because the truth is, everything doesn't feel okay. I feel like I'm just struggling to keep my head above water, and it's exhausting. (pausing, looking up) And the crying... it's just like, my body's way of releasing all the emotions that I've been holding in. Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just sitting there, feeling so overwhelmed and sad. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'm just feeling so much pain and sadness, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, feeling tears start to fall) I guess that's why I'm here, though... to try to figure out how to make it stop, and to find a way to be happy again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pause, looking down, feeling a sense of shame and vulnerability) Yes... I have had those thoughts. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) It's hard to admit, but... sometimes when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, I'll have these fleeting thoughts of... of not wanting to be here anymore. (looking up, feeling tears in my eyes) It's not like I've ever actually considered doing anything, or made any plans... but the thoughts are there, and they scare me. (pausing again, feeling a sense of fear and uncertainty) I don't know where they come from, or why I have them... but they feel like they come out of nowhere, and they're just so... overwhelming. (looking down, feeling a sense of shame) I feel like I'm a bad person for even thinking those things, like I'm not a good mom or a good person. (pausing, taking a deep breath) But at the same time... I feel like I need to be honest about it, because maybe that's the only way I can get help. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I don't want to feel this way anymore, I want to be happy and healthy, and I want to be a good mom to my baby. (pausing, feeling tears fall) I just don't know how to make it stop, and that's why I'm here.

be here anymore' when feeling overwhelmed and sad, which aligns with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)

The EPDS score of 28 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's reports of <quote>feeling overwhelmed</quote>, <quote>difficulty coping with daily responsibilities</quote>, and <quote>thoughts of self-harm</quote> are particularly concerning. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if experiencing suicidal thoughts
3. Develop a safety plan with the patient to ensure their well-being and the well-being of their baby
4. Recommend <med>support groups</med> or <med>online resources</med> for <med>postpartum depression</med> and <med>anxiety</med>
5. Encourage patient to engage in <med>self-care activities</med> and <med>relaxation techniques</med> to manage stress and anxiety

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 28: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient, a postpartum individual, presented with a range of emotional and behavioral concerns that warrant further evaluation. The main symptoms expressed include:

* Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities
* Difficulty coping with daily responsibilities and caring for their baby
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood, with reports of lying awake at night due to racing thoughts and worries
* Feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and self-blame
* Crying spells and emotional reactivity

Consistent patterns across answers include a pervasive low mood, loss of enjoyment in activities, and significant anxiety. The patient reported feeling overwhelmed, struggling to cope with the demands of motherhood, and experiencing persistent sadness.

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Difficulty coping with daily responsibilities

Specific risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* **Safety concern:** The patient reported having thoughts of self-harm, which requires immediate attention and follow-up.

**Screening Observation Summary:**
This patient presents with a range of symptoms and concerns that suggest a potential risk for postpartum depression and anxiety. The reported feelings of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, combined with sleep difficulties and feelings of worthlessness, warrant further evaluation and follow-up. The presence of thoughts of self-harm is a significant safety concern that requires immediate attention and support. Referral for further assessment and potential treatment is recommended to ensure the patient's safety and well-being.
